summary.title: OmniOpt: Taxonomy, Geometry, and Benchmarking of Modern Optimizers

details: Over one hundred modern optimizers are described in incompatible local vocabularies (moment estimators, preconditioners, projections, sign maps, wrappers), so it is unclear where two methods intervene, whether their mechanisms compose, and which training objective each actually improves.
Empirical optimizer claims are highly protocol-sensitive, so single-number leaderboards do not transfer across scale, context length, architecture, or tuning budget.

OmniOpt: a coupled survey-and-benchmark framework that treats every optimizer as a structured transformation of a stochastic training signal through a five-stage meta-pipeline (parameter scoping/routing, gradient transformation, state evolution, update reconstruction, update finalization), with the claim that most methods are sparse (one- or two-stage) modifications of this shared pipeline.

A norm-constrained linear-minimization-oracle (LMO) view is used to unify update directions (sign = L-infinity ball, Muon = spectral-norm polar map / Gram preconditioner, Adam = adaptive box), yielding a four-axis decomposition: update domain, state estimator, geometry-and-precondition operator, finalization wrapper.

A dual-dimension taxonomy assigns each of 108 optimizers one primary mechanism family (T1 element-wise adaptive/scalar control, T2 matrix-structural, T3 sign/discretization, T4 state compression, T5 curvature-aware/geometric regularization) plus multi-label effect objectives (O1 convergence, O2 per-step cost, O3 memory, O4 stability, O5 hyperparameter robustness, O6 generalization), which then define the benchmark's evaluation axes.
Stage 1: short-context screening on C4 with LLaMA-style models at 60M, 130M, 350M, 1B parameters, with only optimizer hyperparameters tuned (architecture, data, schedule held fixed).
Stage 2: FineWeb-Edu long-context pretraining at 340M and 1B, with context lengths spanning 256 to 32k tokens.
Cross-domain check: CIFAR100 image classification with ResNet50, DeiT-S, and CAFormer-S12 backbones.
Four LM architectures spanning standard and linear attention: Transformer++, GLA, DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet.

24 representative optimizers chosen to cover regions of the four-axis space, spanning T1 (AdamW, RAdam, NAdam, Adan, AdaBelief, Prodigy, MARS-AdamW), T2 (Muon, RMNP, SOAP, Shampoo, MARS-Shampoo, GaLore), T3 (Lion, MARS-Lion), T4 (APOLLO, Conda, 8-bit Adam, CAME, AdaFactor, Adam-mini), T5 (AdamP, LAMB, Sophia); AdamW is the reference baseline.
Quality via validation perplexity plus Stage-2 downstream Commonsense Reasoning average over ten tasks (ARC-E/C, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ, COPA, LAMBADA-OpenAI, SciQ).

Efficiency via per-step optimizer runtime and optimizer-state memory; stability via gradient-norm dynamics; robustness via local learning-rate perturbation; generalization via cross-scenario/cross-architecture transfer and mean rank.
Results are aggregated at the optimizer, family (T1-T5), and axis levels rather than as a single leaderboard.

Mechanistic ablation of Muon: removal of the diagonal second moment, Newton-Schulz orthogonalization, two-way learning-rate scaling, placement of Nesterov momentum before vs. after orthogonalization, and finalization choices, cross-validated across model scales and architectures.
Tuned per-scale learning rates and method-specific settings (e.g., projection ranks 128-1024 and refresh intervals for GaLore/APOLLO/Conda) reported for reproducibility.

key_findings.finding: No optimizer dominates the multi-objective frontier; the practical question is which mechanism matches the binding constraint of a run.
key_findings.evidence: Across Stage-1/Stage-2 runs, SOAP gives the best perplexity and the most transferable cross-architecture quality (top mean rank, e.g. best PPL on Transformer++ 340M at 23.90 vs AdamW 24.62 and on 1B at 18.72 vs 18.90) but incurs the highest per-step runtime and memory; AdaFactor/8-bit Adam save memory without changing direction; APOLLO wins at short context but collapses at long context.

key_findings.finding: Spectral orthogonalization is the indispensable core of Muon-style matrix optimizers, while the surrounding gain operations are secondary and order-sensitive.
key_findings.evidence: In the Muon ablation, removing the diagonal second moment alone raises perplexity from 17.78 to 70.74, whereas replacing it with Newton-Schulz orthogonalization recovers and surpasses the AdamW baseline at 16.86; accumulating momentum in the orthogonalized space or scaling the learning rate before orthogonalization degrades results.

key_findings.finding: Aggressive optimizer-state compression is rank-bounded: short-context gains do not certify long-context behavior.
key_findings.evidence: APOLLO is the single best optimizer at 256-token context but the worst at 32k, degrading by +21.87 PPL, roughly three times the AdamW baseline degradation; explained as a fixed low-dimensional projection discarding proportionally more information as gradient effective rank grows with context.

key_findings.finding: Gains come from geometry-sensitive direction maps and the structured state feeding them, not from element-wise refinements of the AdamW template.
key_findings.evidence: Under matched retuning, RAdam, NAdam, AdaBelief and Prodigy fall into the weakest tuned-perplexity tier, and diagonal-curvature or trust-ratio wrappers (Sophia, LAMB) are weak or only situationally competitive despite extra cost, while Kronecker-basis (SOAP) and variance-reduced (MARS-AdamW, the most stable AdamW-style enhancement in Stage 2) methods improve consistently.

key_findings.finding: Composability is governed by locality on the pipeline/axes: mechanisms in different stages stack, same-slot mechanisms conflict or need explicit ordering, and spectral geometry gains are architecture-conditional.
key_findings.evidence: Variance reduction (Axis II) composes with AdamW/Lion/Shampoo bases; low-rank projection (S2/S4) composes with state quantization (S3/S4) as in Q-GaLore; whereas two S2 matrix constraints (orthogonalization vs projection) and LOMO-style fused updates conflict; empirically, Muon gain operations that stack on Transformer++ across scales stop improving beyond the best single gain on Gated DeltaNet.
